Let H, C, and T be the sets of customers whose meals contain ham, cheese, and tomato. Every sandwich has two of these ingredients, so every customer's meal contains at least two of them. Each customer therefore belongs to at least one pairwise intersection, and the total is the size of the union of the three pairwise intersections.

By inclusion-exclusion, with $|H\cap C\cap T| = 20$:

$$|(H\cap C)\cup(H\cap T)\cup(T\cap C)| = 80 + 90 + 100 - 3(20) + 20 = 230$$

Check by exact counts: customers with exactly two ingredients are $(80-20)+(90-20)+(100-20)=60+70+80=210$, and the 20 customers with all three bring the total to $210+20=230$.

ANSWER: 230
